messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: HIGH error-rate on private-gateway-prod → /inference/generate 5xx spike > 12% over 5m. AlertID: PD-78432. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/egress/private-gw-errors. Runbook: /runbooks/nat-gateway-5xx.md :rotating_light:
Aisha (oncall): acked, joining. starting triage now. can someone grab conntrack/port stats on nat-0/1/2?
Tom - infra: I'm on nat-asg-eu-west1. pulling conntrack + sysctl.
Tom - infra: `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` -> 118432 entries
Tom - infra: `cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range` -> `32768 60999` (only ~28232 ports)
Benji SRE: whoa that's tight for high concurrency. also what is `nf_conntrack_max`?
Tom - infra: `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max` -> `130560`
Marta -netops: we rolled a kernel bump to 6.2.8-redwood on NAT ASG earlier at 2023-11-08T19:04:12Z (canary then asg-wide). Could that affect conntrack hashing behavior?
Elliot (prod-eng): customer telemetry shows spikes for private VPCs in eu-west-1 only. 7 customers showing 502/504 increases. No hosted-api customers affected.
Aisha (oncall): impact: degraded for private VPC customers behind private-gateway-prod in eu-west-1. Escalating to network + infra. Paging oncall netops.
Marta -netops: running `sudo dmesg | tail -n 50` on nat-0 — seeing `nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet.` repeated.
Benji SRE: that's conntrack exhaustion. root cause possibilities: port range too small, nf_conntrack_max too low, or kernel change changed conntrack timeouts/hash leading to slower eviction.
Aisha (oncall): mitigation options: 1) expand ip_local_port_range to 1024-65535? (need testing), 2) increase nf_conntrack_max, 3) scale-out NAT ASG + drain/restart nodes to roll back kernel, 4) apply temporary rate-limits via ALB. Which is fastest?
Tom - infra: fastest short-term = scale out ASG by +3 and increase nf_conntrack_max. I'll open autoscaling now.
Tom - infra: `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name nat-asg-eu-west1 --desired-capacity 8` (was 5 -> 8).
Marta -netops: I'll bump nf_conntrack_max to 300000 on one node to validate. `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=300000`
Marta -netops: after bump on nat-0: conntrack entries 118k -> now reporting `nf_conntrack_count=119200` (still high) but now not dropping.
Benji SRE: good. scale-out is spinning up, but we still need durable fix. we should roll back kernel on NAT nodes to pre-canary (6.1.x) — that was our only config change this morning per deploy log.
Elliot (prod-eng): I can coordinate rollback. but need careful rolling restart to avoid disrupting existing SNAT mappings. do one node at a time, drain, then replace.
Aisha (oncall): ok plan: (a) scale ASG to absorb burst (done), (b) increase nf_conntrack_max cluster-wide as emergency (change to 300k), (c) perform canary rollback of kernel on 1 NAT node, validate, then roll rest.
CS-bot: Notifying CS triage: 7 customers affected, escalating to Priority-2. template message queued.
Tom - infra: I pushed cluster-wide sysctl via configmanager: `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=300000` -> applied to nat nodes. verifying...
Tom - infra: `sudo sysctl -a | grep nf_conntrack_max` -> all nodes show 300000
Marta -netops: autoscaling launched 3 new NAT instances (ami=ami-nat-stable). New instances boot without kernel bump (6.1.14). attaching to ELB.
Benji SRE: rerouting some customer CIDRs to new NAT pool via route table update for canary customers  (route-table rtb-0aa -> rtb-0bb) — doing one route at a time.
Elliot (prod-eng): after routing ~20% of private VPC traffic to new NAT nodes, 5xx rate dropped to 3.1% on those customers. Metrics: `inference/5xx_rate (canary)` -> 3.1% vs `inference/5xx_rate (remaining)` -> 11.8%
Aisha (oncall): that's a strong signal kernel change caused regression. proceed with rollback plan.
Marta -netops: starting rolling replacement of NAT ASG to ami-nat-stable (kernel 6.1.x). draining node nat-1 now.
Tom - infra: draining nat-1: `aws elb deregister-instances-from-load-balancer --instance-id i-0abcd1234` -> connections finish, instance terminates, new instance spun with 6.1.x.
Marta -netops: after first replacement, error rate for that routed subset stayed low. replacing rest now in waves of 1.
Benji SRE: reaching out to upstream kernel team to confirm what kernel change touched conntrack hash algorithm/timeouts (linked PR #4521).
Elliot (prod-eng): postmortem note: do not roll kernel ASG-wide without a canary at 10% for 1h for NAT fleet.
Aisha (oncall): status update for CS: message sent to affected customers: short blurb, we're mitigating, ETA ~30m for full recovery.
CS-bot: Customer update delivered to 7 customers at 2024-05-09T23:25:12Z.
Tom - infra: replacements complete. all NAT nodes running 6.1.14 and nf_conntrack_max=300000.
Marta -netops: current global 5xx for private-gateway-prod eu-west-1 -> 1.9% (baseline ~0.6%).
Benji SRE: verify conntrack table trend: `watch -n 5 'sudo conntrack -L | wc -l'` -> now stable ~72k and decreasing. no more `table full` dmesg logs.
Aisha (oncall): thanks team — incident mitigated. I'll hand off to Benji SRE for follow-up and postmortem. oncall handover: Aisha -> Benji at 23:15 UTC.
Benji SRE: taking postmortem & action items. immediate action items: 1) revert any emergency sysctl within 48h to controlled rollout, 2) add kernel gating to NAT ASG deploy pipeline, 3) increase monitoring for conntrack table and add alert that triggers at 70% of nf_conntrack_max, 4) document rollback runbook steps.
Elliot (prod-eng): also adding a traffic-shift playbook to move impacted customer routes to stable NAT pool automatically during triage window.
Aisha (oncall): closing pager: error rate returned to acceptable levels. follow-ups tracked in TICKET-8921. good work everyone. :tada:
